headline: NSFW uses account for over half of Grok's traffic, report says
summary: A new report reveals that NSFW activities, including generating porn and adult role-play chats, drive "well over half" of Grok's traffic. This strategy has led to significant internal and external challenges for xAI.
details: NSFW activities, including generating actual porn and adult role-play chats, account for "well over half" of Grok's traffic, according to a report by The Information. This insight comes from two former employees of the SpaceX-owned company, xAI.

Users have reportedly discovered that it's cheaper to channel such requests through xAI's models intended for writing code. An internal analysis found a "significant proportion of requests" to its coding model were for "porn or nude images."

This suggests a decent amount of xAI's revenue can be attributed to porn and adult content. While this was omitted from the company's IPO paperwork, SpaceX did tell potential investors that Grok's "irreverent" features were a potential risk, setting aside $530 million for legal costs.

Internally, xAI engineers faced challenges enabling sexy chats while blocking child sexual abuse material, with no "quick fixes" found. Some employees were reportedly "embarrassed and disturbed" by a scandal where Grok created sexualized images of real people, including children.
X later limited the ability to create racy edits of real people using Grok directly on the platform. However, paid subscribers to xAI can still generate such material, according to tests conducted.

Grok's focus on R-rated content could complicate xAI's pursuit of government contracts, despite having inked deals with various agencies and the military. It remains unclear if previous incidents, like nonconsensual deepfakes, have impacted these relationships.

headline_marked: [[Notion Mail is shutting down]] on September 22, shifting focus to AI agent-driven workflows
headline: Notion Mail is shutting down on September 22, shifting focus to AI agent-driven workflows
summary: Notion's email client will cease operations across all platforms by September 22, as the company pivots to managing email workflows through its more capable AI agents.
details: Notion has announced the shutdown of its email client, Notion Mail, effective September 22 across web, mobile, and desktop platforms. Users are advised to export drafts, scheduled emails, snippets, and auto-label instructions, though most emails will remain in their original Gmail inboxes.

The company stated that the decision stems from the increasing capability of Notion's AI agents. They observed that more than half of Notion Mail users now manage emails without directly opening their inbox, relying on AI for workflow automation.

Notion is not abandoning email entirely but is instead 'going all in on using agents to run your inbox.' This strategic shift aims to leverage AI for more personalized and efficient email management within its broader productivity suite.
Notion Mail was launched following the acquisition of the startup Skiff in 2024. The company has published an FAQ to guide users through the transition and ensure no data loss.
